meta.title: CANDIDATE — Remote Delegate and Gateway ownership

boundaries.label: Device A role — shared OS account boundary
Device B role — shared OS account boundary

cards.title: Separate authoritative owners
items: Gateway Registry schema 10 owns immutable device ownership, current access policy, request correlations, execution reservations and durable CLI-routing permits. Legacy devices retain explicit project grants; login never adopts them. Explicit migration removes obsolete duplicate execution ceilings without rewriting frozen operation history.

Native owns its service host. The public Gateway deviceclient SDK embeds the connector runtime and joins Serve before releasing identity. Expected SDK shutdown requires qualified Serve cancellation and clean Close; it proves neither task closure nor a successful connection.

The local profile owns workspace approvals, credentials and legacy alias pins. Native alone owns provider/model/effort support, permissions, budgets, defaults, validation, admission, sessions, lifecycle and accepted outcomes. Gateway forwards immutable intent; discovery remains dated advice.

cards.title: Enrollment and transport
items: Optional device_login exposes a public descriptor plus authenticated self-enrollment and owner revocation. Verified device:enroll and live owner policy gate enrollment; replacement also requires device:manage and exact prior generation. OAuth/headless or private-token flows preserve CSR/request identity.

Public HTTPS OAuth/JWKS and device mTLS WSS have separate trust roles. Negotiated v1 preserves legacy aliases; v2 adds scope-relative filesystem/selection and root-addressed controls. Native public-contract version remains 1. Devices initiate WSS; Gateway sees plaintext. Session owners close sockets before canceling read/write contexts and join parent-cancellation hooks before reporting done; independent close errors remain visible.

Verified token scopes intersect current owner policy or legacy grants. New work also needs current local scope approval. Revocation denies authority without proving task closure. Approved workspace and automatic OS temp scopes are routing boundaries in one trusted account, never an OS sandbox.

cards.title: Browse, select and preserve intent
items: Normal flow: list_workspaces, list_directory, read_file and inspect_git, then get_capabilities for an explicit device/scope-relative directory. Native alone reads through rooted descriptors. Reads allocate no project, pin, task or admission namespace. Git candidates are structural observations; requested names and bytes remain exact response data, excluded from diagnostics.

Native supplies automatic whole OS temp scopes: Linux /tmp; macOS per-user temp and shared /private/tmp, canonicalized and deduplicated. New selection retains no alias pin. Current local approval is leased through CLI Start, then released before Wait. Native preserves directory custody and canonical-path semantics; same-path replacement does not move a running cwd.

prepare_dispatch preserves a saved client request ID, selector and Native option omissions. Replay lookup precedes live selection and identity allocation. prepare_continuation freezes one typed successor and exact predecessor guards; Native alone decides saved-session eligibility. dispatch_task confirms either existing draft without silent failover.

Legacy resolve_project retains its first exact pin; changed selectors conflict. Legacy local pins include tombstones: 1,024 records and 4 MiB encoded data, without eviction; Gateway retains its separate 1,024/device resolution bound. Periodic v2 metadata carries at most 100 workspaces and a dated legacy pin budget, never all retained projects. Legacy physical bindings and strict Native root/credential/process guards retain their existing semantics.

cards.title: Recovery conserves two ledgers
items: Full prior-fleet coverage precedes every routed CLI. Census/ACK or explicit out-of-band prior-CLI join attestation binds current credential, process boot and exact generation; neither supplies task closure.

Routing permits remain through actual Wait/output cleanup. Only closed older routing rows compact; active controls and uncertain execution reservations remain held. Execution release requires canonical closure, exact confirmed stop or permanent refusal.

Restore persists barriers before canonical inventory, mapping/drain and guarded reopen. Compact immutable Origin binding restores existing-task correlations and permanent refusal tombstones; malformed or wrong-owner bindings reject the whole page. Requested options remain only in the retained request body. Body disposal permits historical controls and existing-only recovery, never fresh admission. Recovery-only cannot admit/resume/reopen; owned-root initialization cannot bypass active fleet restore.

cards.title: Source and acceptance scope
items: External Native nodes cite Gateway consumer contracts, not Native implementation. Repository metadata must identify Root's real source checkpoint before rendering. Namespace, filesystem, scoped-model, execution-option, project-hash, Origin-binding and continuation features are checked where required; missing support fails explicitly.

This candidate is not release-ready. The dated Linux actual-process filesystem and compact-dispatch fixture proofs do not establish installed-provider continuation, native macOS, physical-network, Cloud-client or seven-day usability acceptance. Later protected-message sizing changes are outside that process checkpoint. Complete engineering gates and final independent review remain pending; docs/verification.md owns evidence.
